subject: modal measurable logics
statement: The paper defines a modal formalism called modal measurable logics for infinitary classical logic with measure-theoretic applications.

subject: Kripke-like semantics
statement: The paper introduces a Kripke-like semantics for modal measurable logics in measurable spaces with a designated modal sigma-ideal.

subject: modal measurable logics
statement: The paper proves completeness of modal measurable logics with respect to the new measurable-space semantics using a modal extension of the Loomis-Sikorski theorem.

subject: intuitionistic monotone modal logic
statement: The paper provides a semantic characterisation for natural extensions of IM in terms of constructive neighbourhood models.

subject: intuitionistic monotone modal logic
statement: The paper presents a calculus for IM and its extensions and proves decidability of IM.

subject: additive and normal formulas
statement: The paper provides a complete description of all additive and normal formulas in K, GL, Grz, S4, and S5.

subject: additive and normal formulas
statement: The paper describes all additive and normal formulas with parameters for K, GL, and S5.

subject: IK-bisimulation
statement: The paper defines the notion of IK-bisimulation between relational semantics for the intuitionistic modal logic IK.

subject: intuitionistic modal logic
statement: The paper proves that IK arises as the IK-bisimulation-invariant fragment of intuitionistic first-order logic.

subject: intuitionistic first-order logic
statement: The paper provides an intrinsic characterisation of IK via a Hennessy-Milner-style theorem.

subject: first-order model theory
statement: The paper develops intuitionistic first-order model theory including intuitionistic analogues of Los's Theorem, elementary embeddings, and countable saturation.

subject: relevant and modal logics
statement: The paper develops translations from relevant logics into normal modal logics to clarify structural connections.

subject: modal operators from halo
statement: The paper defines a parametric family of modal operators from the halo by varying nonstandard witnesses.

subject: halo-derived modalities
statement: The paper identifies four canonical instances of halo-derived operators, including topological closure, Cantor derivative, and the ω-accumulation point operator.

subject: modal logic completeness
statement: The paper proves that K4 is the complete logic over infinite spaces.

subject: modal logic completeness
statement: The paper proves that GL is the complete logic over infinite ω-scattered spaces.

subject: Schreier graphs of Z² shifts
statement: The paper proves that the continuous oriented chromatic number of F(2^Z²) is 7.

subject: Schreier graphs of Z^n shifts
statement: The paper proves that the Borel and measurable oriented chromatic number of F(2^Z^n) is 5 for n>1.

subject: Lindenbaum-algebras
statement: The paper introduces generalizations of representations of integers modulo p in the form of decidable Lindenbaum-algebras.

subject: diophantine inequalities
statement: The paper shows that if a system of diophantine inequalities is not solvable in a Lindenbaum-algebra, then it is not solvable over the standard integers.

subject: Q-spaces and Δ-spaces
statement: The paper proves that the existence of a measurable cardinal, crowded Baire spaces of certain types, and measure-bearing topological spaces are equiconsistent.

subject: Lindelöf Q-spaces
statement: The paper proves that if X is a T_3 Lindelöf Q-space with w(X)≤c, then |X|<cf(c).

subject: modal-temporal language
statement: The paper analyzes the expressive power of the basic modal-temporal language across five order types and shows two distinct levels of definability.

subject: traceable sets
statement: The paper introduces traceable sets as a classical proxy for definable decision regions in o-minimal structures.

subject: ReLU approximation
statement: The paper proves that characteristic functions of traceable sets in [-1/2,1/2]^n can be approximated in L^p to accuracy ε by ReLU networks of size O(ε^{-p(n-1)/m}).

subject: definable sets
statement: The paper obtains statistical learning rates for binary classification in o-minimal structures with misclassification error O(N^{-m/(m+pn-p)}).

subject: structural completeness
statement: The paper proves that every quasivariety of finite type with CEP generated by finite algebras and containing an infinite irreducible algebra is not strongly structurally complete.

subject: meet-semidistributive varieties
statement: The paper proves that every congruence meet-semidistributive variety of finite type generated by finite algebras is strongly structurally complete if and only if it is tabular.

subject: modal logics
statement: The paper establishes that Dummett's and Medvedev's logics are structurally complete but not strongly structurally complete.

subject: primitive varieties
statement: The paper proves that in primitive congruence-distributive varieties of finite type, the tabular subvarieties, and only those, are strongly primitive.

subject: Polish groups
statement: The paper proves that every homomorphism from a Polish group to a countable torsion-free residually finite group has open kernel.

subject: Grigorchuk group
statement: The paper proves that the Grigorchuk group is a homomorphic image of a nonprincipal ultraproduct of groups if and only if there exists a measurable cardinal.

subject: q-series
statement: The paper formalizes the theory of q-series and basic hypergeometric series in the Lean proof assistant.

subject: Rogers-Ramanujan identities
statement: The paper provides fully verified proofs of the Rogers-Ramanujan identities using Lean.

subject: Jacobi Triple Product
statement: The paper provides a fully verified proof of the Jacobi Triple Product formula using Lean.

subject: Hennessy-Milner theorem
statement: The paper demonstrates that the Hennessy-Milner theorem is equivalent to ACA_0 over RCA_0.

subject: van Benthem characterization
statement: The paper introduces three variants of the van Benthem characterization theorem: semantic, syntactic, and hybrid forms.

subject: van Benthem semantic form
statement: The paper shows that the semantic form of van Benthem characterization is provable in RCA_0.

subject: van Benthem syntactic form
statement: The paper shows that the syntactic form of van Benthem characterization is provable in PRA.

subject: van Benthem hybrid form
statement: The paper shows that the hybrid form is equivalent to the weak completeness theorem for first-order logic over RCA_0.

subject: pseudo-solenoids
statement: The paper shows that homeomorphism groups of all pseudo-solenoids, including the pseudo-circle, have non-metrizable universal minimal flows.

subject: conceptual completeness
statement: The paper characterizes conceptual completeness of a fragment in terms of a duality between theories and topoi.

subject: geometric logic fragments
statement: The paper shows that conceptually complete fragments are conservatively embedded in full geometric logic.

subject: coherent logic
statement: The paper gives a new proof of conceptual completeness for coherent logic.

subject: regular and disjunctive logics
statement: The paper shows that regular, disjunctive, and essentially algebraic logic with falsum are conceptually complete.

subject: unary algebras
statement: The paper provides a counterexample showing that 1-ultrahomogeneous mono-unary algebras being ultrahomogeneous does not generalize to all unary algebras.

subject: unary algebras
statement: The paper shows that locally finite unary algebras with finitely many 1-orbits are ω-categorical in tree-like cases.

subject: Ziegler degrees
statement: The paper shows that the theory of the Ziegler degrees is bi-interpretable with true second-order arithmetic.

subject: sum-product phenomenon
statement: The paper shows a sum-product phenomenon in fields with abstract dimension theories generalizing geometric dimensions.

subject: definable fields
statement: The paper proves that for type-definable sets of positive dimension, non-expansion of sumset and product set implies existence of a definable field.
